note.text: Plate tectonics explains movement of rigid lithospheric plates and many associated landforms. Divergent boundaries move apart; convergent boundaries move toward one another; transform boundaries slide past. Plates include crust and uppermost mantle. They do not simply equal individual continents: one plate can carry both continental and oceanic areas. Earthquakes and much volcanism occur near boundaries, although not all volcanic activity is exactly on a plate edge. Mantle processes and forces including slab pull contribute to movement.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Plate tectonics explains movement of rigid lithospheric plates and many associated landforms. Divergent boundaries move apart; convergent boundaries move toward one another; transform boundaries slide past. Plates include crust and uppermost mantle. They do not simply equal individual continents: one plate can carry both continental and oceanic areas. Earthquakes and much volcanism occur near boundaries, although not all volcanic activity is exactly on a plate edge. Mantle processes and forces including slab pull contribute to movement.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A class can model boundaries with card pieces: separate them, bring them together and slide them side by side. The model shows relative movement rather than the full physics. Do not use every Cameroonian volcanic feature as proof of a present plate boundary: the Cameroon Volcanic Line requires more specific regional explanation.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify relative movement before predicting the associated process. Convergence can involve subduction or continental collision, depending on plate types. Distinguish a plate from its crustal surface and from a country's political boundary.
